paper_metadata.title: Entity extraction: From unstructured text to DBpedia RDF triples
paper_metadata.abstract: The paper presents an end-to-end system that extracts RDF triples describing entity relations and properties from unstructured text. The pipeline includes semantic parsing and coreference resolution, groups actions and properties across sentences using coreference chains, processes more than 114,000 Wikipedia articles, extracts over 1,000,000 triples, maps 189,000 extracted triples to the DBpedia namespace using bootstrapped ontology mappings, and reports an F1 score of 66.3% on mapped triples.

problem_addressed: The paper addresses the problem of extracting structured entity-relation information from the unstructured text of Wikipedia articles and integrating the extracted information with the DBpedia ontology and namespace. Its objective is to extend DBpedia beyond information already available in infoboxes and other structured or semi-structured article content.

methodology.description: The method is a seven-module pipeline executed in sequence: WikiMarkup filtering; Wikipedia-link extraction; Athena semantic parsing with semantic role labeling; Stanford CoreNLP coreference resolution; mention-to-entity linking using article links and Wikifier; information alignment and entity extraction; and ontology mapping from PropBank predicate-argument roles to DBpedia properties. Semantic-role arguments provide candidate subjects and objects, coreference chains propagate representative entity links across mentions and sentences, and extracted predicates are first represented in the PropBank namespace. The mapping component bootstraps PropBank-to-DBpedia property mappings from matching subject-object pairs in existing DBpedia triples, generalizing entities to DBpedia ontology classes. The resulting mapped triples are serialized as DBpedia RDF N-Triples. The method does not use joint neural extraction, prompting, or fine-tuning; its central mechanisms are linguistic analysis, rules, linking, and bootstrapped schema mapping.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: The system uses the PropBank roleset and predicate-argument schema during semantic parsing, then maps PropBank predicates and argument roles to the DBpedia property ontology. DBpedia URIs and ontology classes constrain entity linking and candidate selection; predicted links whose DBpedia class conflicts with the Stanford named-entity class are pruned. Mapping generalization uses 43 top-level DBpedia ontology classes, plus String, Date, and Number categories.

text_to_kg_stages: Text preprocessing: WikiMarkup filtering removes annotations, link-only sections, references, and markup while retaining running text.
Entity and concept extraction: named entity mentions are obtained from article links, Wikifier, and Stanford CoreNLP annotations.
Entity typing: Stanford named-entity classes are used to filter conflicting linked entities.
Coreference resolution: Stanford CoreNLP creates coreference chains across the text.
Entity resolution and linking: article links and Wikifier mentions are converted to DBpedia URIs and ranked.
Relation and triple extraction: Athena semantic role labeling identifies PropBank predicates and arguments; binary relations are generated from n-ary predicate-argument structures.
Attribute extraction: temporal AM-TMP expressions are detected with date-pattern regular expressions; location AM-LOC arguments are linked to place entities.
Ontology or schema mapping: PropBank predicate-argument roles are mapped to DBpedia properties using bootstrapped mappings.
Graph construction: mapped subject-predicate-object records are serialized as DBpedia RDF N-Triples.
Knowledge fusion and deduplication: extracted triples are compared with existing DBpedia triples and repeated or already-present triples are identified.

input_output.input_type: Unstructured natural-language text from English Wikipedia articles after removal of WikiMarkup.
input_output.input_granularity: Wikipedia articles processed at article and sentence level; the evaluation samples individual sentences, while coreference and extraction operate over article text.
input_output.output_representation: Subject-predicate-object RDF triples, with entities represented by DBpedia URIs, predicates mapped to DBpedia properties when possible, and literals including dates, years, integers, and strings; outputs are stored in N-Triple format.

evaluation.setting: Manual evaluation of 200 randomly sampled sentences from different Wikipedia articles. Human analysis identified relevant subject-predicate-object triples and compared them with retrieved triples. Attribute values were scored strictly: an extracted attribute had to exactly match the corresponding sentence attribute. Large-scale processing was performed on 114,895 articles over approximately five days using a cluster of 10 machines.

value: The system processed 114,895 articles containing 2,156,574 sentences and extracted 1,023,316 triples.
Of the extracted triples, 189,610 were mapped to the DBpedia ontology; 15,067 of these already existed in DBpedia, while 174,543 were new triples in the DBpedia namespace.
The extracted mapped triples achieved 74.3% precision, 59.9% recall, and 66.3% F1 on the 200-sentence manual evaluation sample.
The largest error source was predicates at 46.4%, followed by subjects at 27.2% and objects at 26.4%.
The system produced approximately one extracted triple for every second processed sentence and nearly nine triples per article.

value: Author-claimed strength: The method provides an end-to-end pipeline that combines semantic parsing, coreference resolution, entity linking, entity extraction, and ontology mapping.
Author-claimed strength: It integrates extracted facts directly with the DBpedia namespace instead of introducing a separate semantic structure.
Experimental strength: The system demonstrates large-scale processing over more than 114,000 articles and produces over one million triples.
Review-level inference: Explicit handling of coreference chains allows properties and relations expressed across multiple sentences to be grouped around the same entity.
Review-level inference: Bootstrapping mappings from existing DBpedia triples enables reuse of learned predicate mappings for entities lacking the original DBpedia property.

evidence.excerpt: We balance precision and recall by employing a combination of NLP tools, including semantic parsing, coreference resolution, and named entity linking.
The system includes ... an automatic learning of ontology mappings to link the extracted triples to the DBpedia namespace.
We extracted a total of 1,023,316 triples.

value: Experimental weakness: Predicate mapping errors account for 46.4% of extraction errors, making ontology alignment the dominant error source.

Experimental weakness: Entity linking and subject/object resolution remain error-prone because new entities may lack DBpedia URIs, Wikifier may predict an incorrect URI, and coreference mentions may be assigned to the wrong chain.
Methodological weakness: The entity vocabulary is restricted to entities already found in DBpedia, so the system does not introduce new named entities into the ontology.
Review-level inference: The reported evaluation is based on only 200 manually analyzed sentences and does not provide a gold-standard corpus for the full Wikipedia text.
Review-level inference: The mapping abstraction uses only 43 of 320 possible top-level DBpedia classes, which can lose distinctions between semantically different relations.

value: The majority of errors stem from erroneous ontology mappings.
The mapping approach generalizes subjects and objects to only 43 top-level DBpedia ontology classes out of 320 possible classes.
New entities that are not already represented in DBpedia lack corresponding DBpedia URIs.
Incorrect Wikifier links and incorrect coreference chains produce erroneous entity links.
The authors note that a mapping describing a person receiving a thing, such as an award, requires more detailed analysis because the received thing may represent items other than awards.

Author-proposed improvement: Increase bootstrapping data by using links to other datasets such as LinkedMDB.
Author-proposed improvement: Replace the rule-based mapping system with a machine-learning-based system.
Author-proposed improvement: Retrain Wikifier using a more current Wikipedia dump.

Review-level inference: A larger, independently annotated evaluation set would make error estimates more reliable and enable more granular comparison of individual pipeline stages.

evidence.excerpt: Ontology mapping can be improved by using a more fine grained approach to the subject-object generalization.
The current rule-based mapping system could be replaced by a more capable system based on machine learning.
We also believe that retraining the named entity linker and improving filtering of erroneous coreference mentions may increase the results.

value: Accurate mapping from fine-grained PropBank predicate-argument roles to DBpedia properties remains unresolved.
Entity linking remains difficult when mentions are ambiguous, incorrectly linked, or refer to entities absent from DBpedia.
Coreference errors can propagate incorrect entity identities and relations through the pipeline.
The paper leaves open whether unstructured text alone can support creation of sufficiently complete Wikipedia or DBpedia resources.
Review-level inference: The system does not resolve the general problem of ontology/schema evolution when extracted relations do not fit existing DBpedia properties.
